thread:
alex: Quick sync — us-west1-b just had a burst of preemptions during the 10:32 window, spilled ~18% of active requests. Not a single-model hotspot, looks zone-level.
maya: ouch. any impact on SLA for prod customers?
simon: A few latency spikes reported, margin calls for dedicated tenants. We fell back to model-variant v2-quant but some requests timed out.
alex: exact numbers: 18% spill, 65s median recovery for affected shards, 120s tail for some requeues.
jules: are we sure it was zone-only and not kernel-level networking issues? logs?
li: autoscaler shows a sequence of preemptions + instance drain in cloud logs. eviction_reason="preemptible_preempt" x3 across the AZ.
ops-bot: alert: evict-surge detected in us-west1-b — preemptible churn rate 0.23/min; applied hedge policy: warm-hedge (10%), fanout=2
maya: good that the bot kicked in. two quick things: 1) how fast can we switch routing policy to prefer multi-zone spread? 2) can we downshift model variants automatically instead of requeueing?
simon: we already have variant-downshift concept in planning. idea: if eviction rate > threshold AND latency budget tight, route to a smaller quantized variant instead of requeue. reduces tokens but keeps tail low.
alex: yes — prefer "variant-downshift" for non-SLA-critical routes. For premium customers we should prioritize region failover to dedicated capacity first.
jules: proposal: add a policy tier matrix.

- premium: prefer dedicated/reserved > zone failover > region failover > variant-downshift
- standard: prefer region failover > variant-downshift > requeue
- free/dev: variant-downshift > best-effort requeue

li: config snippet I tested locally:

```
routing_policy:
  churn_threshold: 0.15
  zone_hedge_pct: 0.12
  variant_downshift: true
  downshift_rules:
    - cpu_pct>70 -> v2-quant
    - evict_rate>0.2 -> v1-4bit
```

simon: keep in mind model-quality gates — we must check eval pass rates before auto-downshift for production prompts.
maya: yes, tie to eval set: if downshift causes >2% bleu/rouge degradation on monitored prompts -> alert and skip.
ops-bot: note: warm-hedge pool has limited capacity in apac-east, will not scale instantly.
alex: to avoid requeues, we should also try concurrent fanout to N regions with fast cancel on success. fanout costs more tokens but reduces tail.
jules: can we make fanout selective by customer tier? only for premium and for ops-critical routes.
li: autoscaler patch I pushed: decreases graceful drain timeout from 90s -> 40s when preempt-rate>0.2. reduces request stall.
simon: dropping drain timeout helps but can increase KV cache loss; consider adding short-lived snapshotting for KV cache to S3 for quick warm-up.
maya: tradeoffs noted. what's the rollout plan for variant-downshift + tiered fanout?
alex: plan: 1) set downshift opt-in for non-prod for 24h, gather quality metrics. 2) enable tiered fanout for premium in blue-green. 3) tweak autoscaler drain heuristics. 4) add alerting for quality regressions.
jules: timeline?
alex: can do opt-in build today, test tomorrow, small prod canary Fri.
li: I'll update the autoscaler PR to include a feature flag `zone_hedge_v2` and add rollout switches.
simon: also add telemetry: per-request path tag: "fallback=variant-downshift" / "fallback=region-failover" so we can slice quality/cost.
ops-bot: reminder: cost impact estimate attached: tiered fanout increases token spend ~4-9% depending on success cancel latency.
maya: predictable. if we combine variant-downshift with caching + batching tweaks, net cost might be neutral or even lower for tail-heavy workloads.
alex: ok folks — action items: li (autoscaler flags + drain timeout change), simon (telemetry + eval gate), maya (quality thresholds), jules (policy matrix + rollout doc). I'll coordinate canary.
li: on it. pushing PR after lunch.
maya: will prepare eval sets and dashboards.
simon: prepping telemetry changes, need a short API for tagging.
jules: drafting rollout doc now. will drop in #eng-release when ready.
alex: thanks. if we see another burst, enable `zone_hedge_v2` and flip standard-tier to prefer variant-downshift.
maya: noted. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: incident closed (auto): evict-surge fell below threshold in us-west1-b — system reverted to baseline routing.
